full_judgment:
Muhammad Ansar Ali J: This Rule arises out of an application of the petitioner Md. Abdus Sobhan under section 339D(1) (b) of the Code of Criminal Procedure for revival of the Sessions Case No. 16 of 1985 under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code of the Court of the Sessions Judge, Barguna against the accused opposite parties 1-7 which was stopped and the accused persons were released under section 339C of the said Code by an order dated 15.4.92 passed by a Division Bench of this Court in Criminal Revision No. 1230 of 1990 (Dhaka) corresponding to Criminal Revision No. 27 of 1987 (Barisal). 

 3. One Md. Adam Ali, Sub-Inspector of Police of Patharghata Police Station while holding investigation in a case being GR Case No. 311 of 1974 got specific information that the victim deceased Amena Begum, wife of accused opposite party No. 2 Hazrat Ali was brutally murdered on 7.3.1983 conjointly by all the seven opposite parties. He therefore lodged a suo motu First Information Report on 23.3.83 with the Patharghata Police Station implicating these accused opposite parties and a case was accordingly started against them under sections 302/34/109 of the Penal Code and the said Sub-Inspector of police on investigation having no prima facie case filed Final Report True in the earlier GR Case No. 311 of 1974 but after completion of the investigation in the subsequent case being Patharghata PS Case No.4 dated 23.3.83 the Investigation Officer was pleased to submit charge-sheet on 20.6.83 against all the accused persons under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code and thereafter the case was sent up to the learned Sessions Judge Patuakhali for trial but meanwhile a new Sessions Division was established at Barguna and the case was transferred to the said new Sessions Division where it was registered and numbered as Sessions Case No. 16 of 1985. The case remained in the court of the learned Sessions Judge, Barguna, from 28.12.1985 till 25.4.87 but the trial could not be concluded, hence an application on behalf of the accused opposite parties under section 339C of the Code of Criminal Procedure was filed before the learned Sessions Judge alleging that the statutory period i.e. 270 days in all, had already expired and the trial could not be concluded within that period and hence under section 339C( 4) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the accused persons were entitled to be released and the proceeding of the case be stopped. But that application was rejected by the learned Sessions Judge by an order dated 2.6.87 with the observation that there was still time for conclusion of the trial. The accused thereafter moved an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure in this Court for quashing the proceeding of the Sessions Case No. 16 of 1985 of the Court of the learned Sessions Judge, Barguna and obtained a Rule in Criminal Revision No. 22 of 1987 at the Barisal Bench of the High Court Division as it was then, but the same was subsequently renumbered as Criminal Revision No. 1230 of 1991 (Dhaka). The said Rule was heard by a Division Bench of this Court on 15.4.92 and the Rule was made absolute in the absence of the lawyer for the State by the following order. 

 "Let the proceeding of Sessions Case No. 16 of 1985 pending in the court of Sessions Judge, Barguna be stopped and the accused persons released under section 339C CrPC" 

 4. Thereafter the petitioner Md. Abdus Sobhan who is a charge-sheet prosecution witness in the said Sessions Case and a full brother of the deceased victim Amena Begum moved this application and obtained the present Rule for revival of the said session’s case. 

 5. Mr. AKM Zahirul Huq, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that the petitioner is an aggrieved person being the full brother of the deceased victim and he has filed the application for revival of the case showing cogent grounds within the statutory period of limitation as required under section 339 D (1) (b) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Therefore the impugned order dated 15.4.92 stopping further proceedings of the Sessions Case and releasing the accused persons should be vacated and the said Sessions Case be revived for trial in the Court of the learned Sessions Judge. Barguna in the interest of justice. 

 6. Before considering the above submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner, it may be pointed out that the provision of section 339D for the revival of the case of the Code of Criminal Procedure was made by Ordinance No. XXIII of 1986 dated 27.3.1986. Section 339 D runs thus: 

 "339D Revival of cases. (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in section 339C, any proceedings in respect of the trial of a case stopped under sub-section (4) of that section shall be revived, if an application for such revival is made by the Government to the Court, where such proceedings were pending on the date they were stopped, within ninety days from that date; and the proceedings thus revived shall continue from the stage at which they were stopped: 

 Provided that where such court is not in existence or has no jurisdiction to try the case for any reason, the application for such revival shall be made to the Court which has jurisdiction to try such case. 

 (2) Where any proceedings are revived under sub-section (1), the accused in the case shall if he is accused of a non-bailable offence, be released on bail to the satisfaction of the Court, unless for reasons to be recorded in writing the court otherwise directs. 

 (3) Where any proceedings are revived under sub-section (1) the trial of the case after such revival shall be concluded within the time specified in sub-section (1) or sub-section (2) of section 339C, as the case may be. 

 (4) If the trial of a case after revival cannot be concluded within the specified times, further proceedings in respect of the trial of the revived case shall stand stopped and the accused persons released. 

 (a) the date of revival of a case shall be deemed to be the date on which the case is received for trial; and 

 (a) where the proceedings of the case were stopped and the accused person released in the Court of a Magistrate, make an application, within sixty days from the date on which the proceedings in respect of the trial of the case have been stopped, to the Sessions Judge. 

 (b) where the proceedings of the case were stopped and the accused person released in the Court of a Sessions Judge, an Additional Sessions Judge, on an Assistant Sessions. Judge make an application, within ninety days from the date on which the proceedings in respect of the trial of the case have been stopped, to the High Court Division, for revival of the case and the Sessions Judge or, as the case may be, the High Court Division may pass thereon such orders as he or it thinks fit. 

 (2) Where the Sessions Judge or, as the case may be, the High Court Division orders for revival of the case, proceedings thereof shall continue from the stage they were stopped in the Court where such proceedings were pending on the date they were stopped, and where such Court is not in existence or has no jurisdiction to try the case for any reason, the proceedings shall continue in the Court which has jurisdiction to try the case. 

 (3) Where any case is revived under sub-section (2) the accused in the case shall, if he is accused of a non-bailable offence, be released on bail to the satisfaction of the Court where the case has been revived, unless for reasons to be recorded in writing, the Court otherwise directs 

 (3A) where any case is revived under sub-section (2) the trial of the case after such revival shall be concluded within the time specified in section 339C." 

 8. From a reading of the aforesaid provisions of section 339D introduced by Ordinance XXXIII of 1986 it appears that the proceedings stopped under section 339C CrPC shall be revived if an application under section 339D (I) is filed by the Government alone to the Court where such proceedings were pending on the date they were stopped, within 90 days from that date and the proceedings thus revived shall continue from the stage at which those were stopped. But by the subsequent amendment in 1991 as mentioned above, the application for revival under section 339D of the Code of Criminal Procedure can be filed by the Government as well as by any aggrieved person, of course on cogent grounds. In respect of the case stopped in the Court of the Magistrate, the application be made within 60 days from the date of stopping the proceedings before the learned Sessions Judge concerned but in case of the proceeding stopped and the accused persons released in the court of the Sessions Judge, Additional Sessions Judge or Assistant Sessions Judge, the application for revival of the case be made under section 339D (1) (b) of the Code within 90 days from date of stopping the proceeding, to the High Court Division. It appears that there has been further amendment of the provision of section 339D of the Code of Criminal Procedure by Act 16 of 1991 dated 5.5.1991 and by this amendment the period of limitation for filing application for revival of the case under section 339D (1) (a) of the Code to the court of the Sessions Judge is 30 days in place of 60 days and that of such application under section 339D (1) (b) of the Code of Criminal Procedure for filing to the High Court Division is 60 days, instead of 90 days. Other provisions of this section remained almost the same. Of course; lastly, by another amendment by Act 42 of 1992 section 339 D altogether has been repealed with some saving clauses in sections 6 and 7 of the said Second Amendment Act. 

 9. From a reading of the earlier provisions of section 339D CrPC, it appears that it was almost a rule and routine matter for revival of the cases stopped under section 339C (4) CrPC on the application of the Government within the period as prescribed and there was no provision for any other person to file any application for revival of such cases. But by subsequent amendment the scope for filing application for revival of the cases under section 339D CrPC has been extended to any aggrieved person also apart from the Government but such application must be on cogent grounds and be filed within the statutory period of limitation as fixed by subsequent amendment. Therefore, it has to be seen particularly in this case, (1) whether the petitioner is an aggrieved person, (2) whether the application has been filed within the statutory period of limitation ie 60 days from the date of stopping the proceeding and (3) whether there are cogent grounds for revival of the case. 

 10. We have heard the learned Advocate for the petitioner but unfortunately, in spite of the service of notice of this Rule upon the accused opposite parties, there is none to appear on behalf of them in this case. In the Rule, State was also made an opposite party; hence we have invited the learned Deputy Attorney-General Mr. Amirul Kabir Chowdhury to address us on this matter, The learned Deputy Attorney-General in his submissions admits that earlier, an application for revival of the case could be filed by Government alone but now it can be filed by any aggrieved person also within the period fixed and on cogent grounds. The word cogent was not in the earlier provision. It has been introduced by the subsequent amendment of the Code in 1991. This word 'cogent' of course has not been defined in the statute in question. The learned Deputy Attorney-General however submits that in the absence of any definition or meaning given in the statute, the ordinary dictionary meaning of the word 'cogent' may be adopted. He therefore refers to the book "Words and Phrases" Permanent Edition-Vol. 7A which shows the meaning of the word 'cogent' at page 113 as follows: 

 12. Now, in the above context, let us see whether the learned Advocate for the petitioner has been able to satisfy the requirements of the amendment and section 339D of the Code of Criminal Procedure for revival of the case. So far the 'locus standi' is concerned the petitioner being the full brother of the deceased victim and a charge-sheet prosecution witness, is no doubt an aggrieved person and competent to file this application for revival of the case. It further appears that the application was filed for revival of the case within 60 days from the date of stopping the proceeding as required under the law. Let us now only see whether there are cogent grounds for filling this application. It has been contended by the learned Advocate for the petitioner that with the creation of a new Sessions Division at Barguna, the learned Sessions Judge posted there could not remain present regularly as he could not bring his family due to shortage of accommodation and other problems and consequently he could not attend court regularly in spite of his efforts. Next, the Criminal Revision case arising out of the application by the accused for stopping the proceeding was heard ex parte by the concerned Bench of this court only in presence of the learned Advocate for the accused petitioners and nobody represented the State or filed any counter-affidavit controverting the facts of the said application, particularly the wrong calculation of the working days. Thirdly, it is pointed out by the learned Advocate for the present petitioner by reference to Order Nos. 43 and 44 dated 3.2.1986 and 15.2.1986 respectively of the order-sheet of the Sessions case, that on these 2 dates, the learned Sessions Judge holding the trial was absent on leave and in his place one Mr. Samendra Nath Sarker, Assistant Sessions Judge was in-charge only to do the routine work and not to hold the trial of the Sessions Case and from the calculation sheet appearing in the records of the case, it transpires that the period started from 3.2.86 to 15.2.86, that means a period of 12 days was also calculated as working days of the learned Sessions Judge which was not permissible in law, as the learned Sessions Judge was on leave and had this period been excluded from the total period of 273 days as calculated in the list of working days on behalf of the accused petitioners, the working days would be at the relevant time much less than 270 days and the learned Sessions Judge was correct in rejecting the application of the accused petitioners under section 339C with the observation that there was still time for proceeding with the trial of the case according to law. But this material fact could not be brought to the notice of their Lordships of this Court while disposing of the said Criminal Revision case, as a result there has been miscarriage of justice. 

 13. We have heard the learned Advocate for the petitioner and examined his submissions vis-a-vis the materials on record and we are convinced that there are cogent and reasonable grounds for filling this application for revival of this case against the accused opposite parties. 

 14. Mr. Zahirul Huq, the learned Advocate for petitioner, has referred to a decision with regard to stopping the proceeding of a case under section 339C of the Code of Criminal Procedure reported in 38 DLR 205 (Md. Joha alias Shamsuzzoha & another vs. State). In the above decision, it has been observed by their Lordships as follows: 

 "An order of stopping of the proceeding of a case and release of the accused does not amount to either an order of discharge or acquittal. In such cases the order of stopping the proceeding remains pending which may be subsequently revived in accordance with law. 

 Here also the proceeding of the Sessions Case No. 16 of 1985 though stopped under section 339C CrPC are pending proceeding which may be revived under section 339D of the Code of Criminal Procedure as amended. 

 15. For the reasons stated above, we are of the view that it is a fit case for revival at the instance of the petitioner who is undoubtedly an aggrieved person. Apart from that it may be pointed out that the charge against the accused opposite parties is of murder and, in any view of the matter, justice demands that the miscreants of such a case should not go untried and unpunished. 

 16. We therefore allow this application for revival of the case and make the Rule absolute. 

 17. Accordingly, the order dated 15.4.92 by a Division Bench of this Court stopping the proceeding of Sessions Case No. 16 or 1985 is hereby vacated and the proceedings of the said Sessions Case No. 16 of 1985 pending in the court of the learned Sessions Judge, Barguna are revived. The accused opposite parties who have already been released are directed to surrender before the learned Sessions Judge, Barguna and the learned Sessions Judge may however release them on bail to his satisfaction and go on with the trial of the case as expeditiously as possible from the stage where it was stopped. 

 Let the records in this case be sent down at once with a copy of this Judgment.
